Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 92, verse 1–11:

(p-286) Surat al-Layl (The Night)

His statement, exalted is He, ﴿By the night when it covers﴾ has three interpretations:

First: when it grows dark. This is the view of Mujahid.

Second: when it covers and conceals. This is the view of Ibn Jubayr.

Third: when it covers the creatures, enveloping and filling them. This is the view of Qatadah, and this is an oath.

﴿And by the day when it displays itself﴾ has two interpretations:

First: when it shines. This is the view of Mujahid.

Second: when it appears. This is what follows from the view of Ibn Jubayr.

It may also bear a third meaning: when it manifests what is in it of creation. This is a second oath.

﴿And by He who created the male and the female﴾. Al-Hasan said: its meaning is "and by He who created the male and the female," so this is an oath by Allah Himself, exalted is He.

It may also bear a second meaning, and it is more akin to the view of al-Hasan, that its meaning is "and by what He created of the male and the female" (p-287), so that "man" (mun) is implied in meaning and deleted in wording. He distinguished them by their creation from male and female, in contrast to the angels who were not created from male and female. The oath is then by the people of His obedience from among His friends and prophets, and His swearing by them is an honouring and an exaltation of them.

Regarding what is meant by "the male and the female," there are two views:

First: Adam and Eve. This is related by Ibn Isa.

Second: from every male and female.

If it is taken according to the view of al-Hasan, then every male and female is included, of humans and of beasts, because Allah created them all.

If it is taken according to the derivation I mentioned, which I said is more apparent, then every male and female among the children of Adam is meant, excluding the beasts, because they are singled out for the guardianship of Allah and His obedience. This is a third oath: ﴿Indeed your effort is diverse﴾, meaning differing. It has two interpretations:

First: indeed your recompense differs; among you is one rewarded with Paradise, and among you is one punished with the Fire.

Second: indeed your actions differ; among you is a believer and a disbeliever, a righteous one and a wicked one, an obedient one and a rebellious one.

It may also bear a third meaning: indeed your characters differ; among you is one merciful and one hard-hearted, one forbearing and one reckless, one generous and one miserly. It is upon this that the oath falls.

Ibn Mas'ud related that this verse was revealed concerning Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, and concerning Umayyah and Ubayy, the two sons of Khalaf, when they tortured Bilal for his Islam. Abu Bakr bought him, paying his price a cloak and ten ounces, and freed him for the sake of Allah, exalted is He, so this was revealed concerning him.

﴿As for he who gives and fears Allah﴾. Ibn Mas'ud said: he means Abu Bakr.

Regarding His statement ﴿gives﴾ there are three interpretations:

First: from spending his wealth. This is the view of Ibn Abbas.

Second: he guards against the prohibitions of Allah which He forbade. This is the view of Qatadah.

Third: he guards against miserliness. This is the view of Mujahid.

﴿And affirms the best reward﴾ has seven interpretations:

First: by the Oneness of Allah, which is the saying "There is no god but Allah." This is the view of al-Dahhak. (p-288)

Second: by the promise of Allah. This is the view of Qatadah.

Third: by Paradise. This is the view of Mujahid.

Fourth: by the reward. This is the view of Khasif.

Fifth: by the prayer, the zakat and the fasting. This is the view of Zayd ibn Aslam.

Sixth: by what Allah has bestowed upon him. This is the view of Ata'.

Seventh: by the replacement for His giving. This is the view of al-Hasan. The meanings of most of them are close to one another.

﴿We will ease him toward ease﴾ has two interpretations:

First: toward good. This is the view of Ibn Abbas.

Second: toward Paradise. This is the view of Zayd ibn Aslam.

It may also bear a third meaning: We will ease for him the means of goodness and righteousness until performing them becomes easy for him.

﴿And as for he who is miserly and considers himself self-sufficient﴾. Ibn Mas'ud said: he means by this Umayyah and Ubayy, the two sons of Khalaf.

Regarding His statement ﴿is miserly﴾ there are two interpretations:

First: he is miserly with his wealth, which does not last. This is the view of Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan.

Second: he is miserly with the right of Allah, exalted is He. This is the view of Qatadah.

﴿And considers himself self-sufficient﴾ has two interpretations:

First: by his wealth. This is the view of al-Hasan.

Second: from his Lord. This is the view of Ibn Abbas.

﴿And denies the best reward﴾ has the seven interpretations mentioned above.

﴿We will ease him toward hardship﴾ has two interpretations:

First: toward evil from Allah, exalted is He. This is the view of Ibn Abbas.

Second: toward the Fire. This is the view of Ibn Mas'ud.

It may also bear a third meaning: We will make difficult for him the means of goodness and righteousness until performing them becomes hard for him. Upon the revelation of these two verses, Qatadah narrates from Khulayd from Abu al-Darda' that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) (p-289) said: "There is no day on which its sun rises but two angels call out: 'O Allah, give the one who spends a replacement, and give the one who withholds a loss.'" Then he recited ﴿As for he who gives and fears Allah﴾ and the verses that follow it.

﴿And his wealth will not avail him when he falls down﴾ has two interpretations:

First: when he falls into the Fire. This is the view of Abu Salih and Zayd ibn Aslam.

Second: when he dies and falls into his grave. This is the view of Mujahid and Qatadah.

It may also bear a third meaning: when he falls into his misguidance and plunges into his sins.

**Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 92, verses 12–21:**

﴿Indeed, upon Us is guidance.﴾ On this there are two interpretations:

First: We make clear the paths of guidance and misguidance. This was said by Yahya ibn Salam.

Second: The clarification of the lawful and the unlawful. This was said by Qatada.

It may also bear a third meaning: upon Us is the reward for the guidance We have granted.

﴿And indeed, to Us belong the Hereafter and the first (life).﴾ On this there are two interpretations:

First: The reward of this world and the Hereafter. This was said by al-Kalbi and al-Farra'.

Second: Ownership of this world and ownership of the Hereafter. This was said by Muqatil.

It may also bear a third meaning: Allah is the One who recompenses in this world and in the Hereafter.

﴿So I have warned you of a Fire that blazes.﴾ On this there are three interpretations:

First: Its meaning is that it rages (tataghayyazu). This was said by al-Kalbi.

Second: That it blazes (tashta'ilu). This was said by Muqatil.

Third: That it glows intensely (tatawahhaju). This was said by Mujahid, who recited a verse of Ali (may Allah be pleased with him):

*"As if salt had been mixed into it, when it blazes, like carnelian amid the shade."*

﴿None will enter it except the most wretched,﴾ meaning, the one who is wretched (al-shaqiyy).

﴿Who denies and turns away.﴾ On this there are two interpretations:

First: He denies the Book of Allah and turns away from obedience to Allah. This was said by Qatada.

Second: He denies the Messenger and turns away from obeying him.

﴿And no one has a favor with him that is to be repaid,﴾ ﴿except seeking the countenance of his Lord, the Most High.﴾ On this there are two interpretations:

First: No one has a favor with Allah, the Exalted, for which He would recompense him, except that a person does it seeking the countenance of his Lord, so that he deserves recompense and reward for it. This was said by Qatada.

Second: For Bilal, the favor that Abu Bakr had done for him, when he bought him, freed him from slavery and rescued him from torment, was a favor already past, for which Abu Bakr was repaid, except that he sought the countenance of his Lord and His reward. This was said by Ibn Abbas and Ibn Mas'ud.

﴿And he will surely be pleased.﴾ This may bear two meanings:

First: He will be pleased with what he is given, because of its abundance.

Second: He will be pleased with what he is given, because of his contentment, since whoever is content without a gift is more obedient to Allah.

**Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 92, verses 12–21:**

﴿Indeed, upon Us is guidance.﴾ On this there are two interpretations:

First: We make clear the paths of guidance and misguidance. This was said by Yahya ibn Salam.

Second: The clarification of the lawful and the unlawful. This was said by Qatada.

It may also bear a third meaning: upon Us is the reward for the guidance We have granted.

﴿And indeed, to Us belong the Hereafter and the first (life).﴾ On this there are two interpretations:

First: The reward of this world and the Hereafter. This was said by al-Kalbi and al-Farra'.

Second: Ownership of this world and ownership of the Hereafter. This was said by Muqatil.

It may also bear a third meaning: Allah is the One who recompenses in this world and in the Hereafter.

﴿So I have warned you of a Fire that blazes.﴾ On this there are three interpretations:

First: Its meaning is that it rages (tataghayyazu). This was said by al-Kalbi.

Second: That it blazes (tashta'ilu). This was said by Muqatil.

Third: That it glows intensely (tatawahhaju). This was said by Mujahid, who recited a verse of Ali (may Allah be pleased with him):

*"As if salt had been mixed into it, when it blazes, like carnelian amid the shade."*

﴿None will enter it except the most wretched,﴾ meaning, the one who is wretched (al-shaqiyy).

﴿Who denies and turns away.﴾ On this there are two interpretations:

First: He denies the Book of Allah and turns away from obedience to Allah. This was said by Qatada.

Second: He denies the Messenger and turns away from obeying him.

﴿And no one has a favor with him that is to be repaid,﴾ ﴿except seeking the countenance of his Lord, the Most High.﴾ On this there are two interpretations:

First: No one has a favor with Allah, the Exalted, for which He would recompense him, except that a person does it seeking the countenance of his Lord, so that he deserves recompense and reward for it. This was said by Qatada.

Second: For Bilal, the favor that Abu Bakr had done for him, when he bought him, freed him from slavery and rescued him from torment, was a favor already past, for which Abu Bakr was repaid, except that he sought the countenance of his Lord and His reward. This was said by Ibn Abbas and Ibn Mas'ud.

﴿And he will surely be pleased.﴾ This may bear two meanings:

First: He will be pleased with what he is given, because of its abundance.

Second: He will be pleased with what he is given, because of his contentment, since whoever is content without a gift is more obedient to Allah.
